calibration: Printed views are not mutually to scale: 18.69 px/m along the body, 19.3 px/m across it, 19.9 px/m in the front view, each from its own dimension bar.

comparisons: Traced tables regenerated into side and three-quarter renders and inspected beside the photograph. No overlay image was made.
corrections: Stance 0.5 degrees nose up from table 2.2, opposite in sign to the 737: forward door 2.54 to 2.58 m, aft 2.38 to 2.42 m.
Flight deck moved aft to u 3.7 after the overhead panel and a sidewall came through the steep nose.
Window pitch 0.72 m from the photograph; the APM schematic draws 0.95 m.
Seated eye moved from u 3.70 to the published 2.92. Window top lowered from 2.76 to 2.66, matching the pillar head in photograph N401YX, which gives about the published upward view.
The stray post from 1.98 to 2.30 crossed the forward view and is gone: N401YX shows a pillar starting at 2.28, so that post became the windscreen pillar and the post at 2.62 was dropped.

Kit changes: glass clear from the seat and tinted from outside, as on the Bendy airliner. The thick glareshield slab and its large FLIGHT GUIDANCE lettering are replaced by a thin sloped hood with a rolled lip over a slim mode control strip. The panel, floor and overhead take their reach from the nose skin, and a dark coaming lines the inside of the nose.
Published eye stations for four kit types sit 0.8 m ahead of where the kit had put them, and the same bias was removed here.

limitations: Crown between u 1.5 and 2 is interpolated because dimension lines overprint the outline there.
Exterior only: shared interior, refitted but not compared with an E-Jet flight deck.
The pillar's upper end stands at 2.85 against about 2.52 in N401YX, to stay outboard of the pilot on the elliptical section.
Sanity pass only: seating, glass and visibility. The panel, hood and pedestal remain the shared kit interior fitted to the nose, not compared with this type's real flight deck.
